body.summary: Fresh-context audit of P30-I20-W58 (commit d0ef1bb1) against its 2 criteria. Both hold. CR-01 (open watch tail picks up newly-persisted chunks each poll tick): the fix hoists _sync_output_from_store (agent_watch.py:1945) into the state-reactive poll-backstop watcher _on_app_state (agent_watch.py:2019), registered at :1891, calling it UNCONDITIONALLY before the parity early-exit at :2021 -- pre-W58 the tail only backfilled on mount and same-fleet poll ticks hit the early-exit. Sync reads persisted agent.output.chunk lines off the event store, independent of live daemon push. Test test_agent_watch_tail_syncs_new_chunks_from_store_on_poll (test_modes_agent_watch.py:562) passes. CR-02 (store sync + live push never double-render): per-recompose count cursor (agent_watch.py:1775 reset; :1985-1987 advance) plus OutputTail.replace clearing all prior rows incl live-push (output_tail.py:257) on first content sync, plus append_output gated off once store owns the tail (:2129-2130). All 3 refutation orderings (push-then-sync, sync-then-push, cap-shift edge) fail to produce a duplicate. Tests test_output_tail_replace_clears_prior_rows_and_reseeds + poll test (asserts count==1) pass. Verdict pass-with-followups because refutation surfaced one genuine latent defect not covered by either criterion for bounded output.

followups.title: 500-line cap-shift freezes long-spawn watch tails
followups.detail: Count-based cursor (agent_watch.py:1985-1987, len(lines)>cursor) vs the shifting lines[-500:] window (agent_watch.py:722, _OUTPUT_BACKFILL_LIMIT=500) means once a spawn exceeds 500 output lines len(lines) plateaus at 500 while the window shifts forward, so the tail freezes at the first 500-line window and drops later chunks. Use a content/seq identity anchor instead of len().

followups.title: CR-01 has no test through the real _on_app_state poll path
followups.detail: Sole test calls _sync_output_from_store() directly (test_modes_agent_watch.py:591) so the poll-tick wiring at agent_watch.py:2019 is verified by reading, not by a test. Add a test that advances state.json mtime to drive _on_app_state end-to-end.
